meta.name: Beagle First-Year Costs
meta.excerpt: Beagles are one of the more affordable breeds to own. Here's the realistic year-one cost breakdown.
meta.meta_description: Beagle first-year cost breakdown: purchase price, food, vet care, pet insurance, and what fencing and containment might actually cost.

intro.label: Overview
intro.heading: Beagle Ownership Costs — Honest Year-One Numbers
intro.html:
Beagles sit in the affordable tier of dog ownership — smaller food portions, minimal grooming costs, and generally good health over their long lifespan. Year one is the most expensive due to acquisition and setup costs.

The variable most guides miss: fencing. If your current setup isn't Beagle-proof (they dig, squeeze through gaps, and follow their nose under any weak point), the containment upgrade cost is meaningful.

special.label: Hidden Costs
special.heading: What Most Beagle Cost Guides Skip
special.html:
Fencing: Standard 4-foot residential fencing often doesn't contain a motivated Beagle. Adding anti-dig barriers (L-shaped wire mesh at the fence base) and checking for gaps adds $200–$800 to a typical yard setup.

Ear care supplies: Budget $50–$100/year for ear cleaner and cotton balls — a small cost that prevents ear infection treatment costs that run 5–10× higher.

faq.q: How much does a Beagle cost to own per year?
faq.a: After the first-year setup costs, annual costs typically run $1,300–$2,200. Food ($400–$600), routine vet care ($300–$600), and pet insurance ($480–$840) are the main recurring expenses. Ear infection treatment adds $100–$400/year if the weekly cleaning routine isn't maintained.

faq.q: Should I get pet insurance for a Beagle?
faq.a: Yes. Beagles are generally healthy, but IVDD and hypothyroidism are meaningful risks. Insurance at $40–$70/month provides a meaningful safety net. Apply before the first vet visit.

faq.q: Are Beagles from rescues cheaper to own?
faq.a: Lower acquisition cost ($200–$400 adoption fee), same ongoing costs. Many rescue Beagles are adults with known history, which can actually be an advantage for predicting health and temperament.

faq.q: What's the most expensive part of owning a Beagle?
faq.a: For most owners, it's either pet insurance over the long lifespan (12–15 years) or a fencing upgrade if the yard wasn't already Beagle-proof. The good news: per-year running costs are low compared to larger breeds.
